name: Backup runner
purpose: Produces a self-contained snapshot of the store artifact without downtime: the application keeps serving reads and writes while the runner copies the file (SQLite: online-backup API or checkpoint-then-file-copy) or requests an engine-native snapshot (Postgres: pg_basebackup or file-system snapshot). Emits a backupCheckpoint event on completion carrying the artifact path and the ISO-8601 completion timestamp.
responsibilities: Snapshot the store to the requested output path while consumer requests continue to serve. No request may be marked failed on account of the backup operation (AC-5108-1).
Produce an artifact a fresh process can open through the same store facade at the same schema version and read the rows committed at or before the snapshot completion timestamp (AC-5108-2).
Emit exactly one backupCheckpoint event on the store's event log at snapshot completion, carrying the artifact path and the completion timestamp (AC-5108-3, AC-5106-1).
internalStructure: One backup(outputPath) method exposed on the store facade. Under the SQLite engine (ADR-601 default), the implementation opens a second connection in backup mode and uses the online-backup API to stream pages to the output path, or issues a WAL checkpoint and then copies the main file; either way the writer's connection stays available. Under an alternate engine the implementation uses the engine-native equivalent behind the same facade method.

interfaces.name: backup
interfaces.description: store.backup(outputPath) -> Promise<{ artifactPath, completedAt }>; the sole backup entry point on the facade. Emits backupCheckpoint on completion via the store's event sink.

dependencies.name: Store facade
dependencies.description: The backup runner is exposed as a method on the store facade and reuses the facade's event sink for backupCheckpoint emission.

tradeoffs: File-level backup is fast, portable, and cheap to restore (point a compatible build at the file), and it does not require a logical schema-aware dump. The cost is that the artifact is engine-native: a SQLite file is not restorable into a Postgres cluster. Cross-engine migration is out of scope for this blueprint. Projects that need a logical dump alongside the file-level backup add a project-authored dump runner beside this one; the file-level runner remains the primary recovery path.
